clauses.object: Retained accountability coupled with substantive discharge

sources.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.

Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and the integrity of the smart contracts5.

5 Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above and the smart contracts are not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.

For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

clauses.object: Retained accountability and substantive discharge

sources.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.

Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and the integrity of the smart contracts5.

5 Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above and the smart contracts are not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.

sources.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. sources.quote: This circular sets out the requirements under which the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) would consider allowing tokenisation of investment products authorised by the SFC under Part IV of the Securities and Futures Ordinance for offering to the public in Hong Kong.
B.   Requirements for primary dealing of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products

Product providers of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products (Product Providers) should ensure that the underlying products should meet the applicable requirements in the relevant rules and regulations, and product codes (including eligibility of Product Providers, product structure, investment and operational requirements, disclosure and ongoing compliance obligations).

Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should confirm to the SFC that they have at least one competent staff with relevant experience and expertise to operate and/or supervise the tokenisation arrangement and to manage the new risks relating to ownership and technology appropriately.

unresolved.statement: Legacy formula and question are proposed interpretations
Which entity or entities qualify as Product Providers, and how does the requirement apply where several entities provide the product?
What authoritative criteria distinguish ultimate or full responsibility from a contractual acknowledgment of responsibility?
What are the boundaries of management, operational soundness, ownership record keeping and the adopted tokenisation arrangement?
Which internal, outsourced and subcontracted functions, interfaces and records belong to the arrangement?
What period applies, and when does responsibility begin or end during migration, provider replacement, termination and historical-record retention?
What do the applicable product authorities, Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds section 6.8 and Appendix Part A of the Tokenised Securities Circular require?
Can responsibility be defined through sufficiently specific factual relations to encode this predicate without merely renaming the unresolved legal requirement?

Retain the existing conjunction only for its supplied-judgment retention claim. Retained responsibility with defective records can satisfy that predicate without establishing proper performance. Adequate outcomes without independently established retention cannot satisfy it; established loss of retention defeats it. No request does not alter retention. clauses.object: Paragraph 10 as retained accountability coupled with substantive responsibility for sound operation and ownership records

sources.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.

Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and the integrity of the smart contracts5.

5 Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above and the smart contracts are not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.

Product Providers should confirm to the SFC that they have at least one competent staff with relevant experience and expertise to operate and/or supervise the tokenisation arrangement and to manage the new risks relating to ownership and technology appropriately.

clauses.standard: Meaning and evaluative predicates remain proposed
clauses.warrant: This reading gives paragraph 10 substantive assurance content beyond allocation of accountability. A provider that remains the accountable entity but has not secured the required operational soundness or proper records could fail this selected control. The records duty and confirmation/demonstration provisions support that reading, but may instead be separate duties supporting r1. The packet supplies no threshold for failures, reasonable care, remediation or strict liability; it therefore does not justify treating every incident as an automatic breach.

clauses.object: The proposed substantive reading remains plausible but lacks a governing discharge standard. Acquired conduct provisions do not resolve whether paragraph 10 itself requires conduct, achieved outcomes or both. Materially defective records despite adequate supervision and prompt remediation distinguish those possibilities. Successful outcomes cannot substitute for retained accountability; missing facts and conflicting ownership preclude affirmative classification. No executable program is supported.

sources.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.

Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and the integrity of the smart contracts5.

5 Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above and the smart contracts are not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.

Product Providers should confirm to the SFC that they have at least one competent staff with relevant experience and expertise to operate and/or supervise the tokenisation arrangement and to manage the new risks relating to ownership and technology appropriately.

assumptions.statement: The primary-dealing and public-offer scope of the first proposal applies.
A consequential rival reads ultimate responsibility as requiring substantive continuing stewardship, beyond retaining accountability.
Management, operational soundness and ownership record keeping include relationships between components where those relationships affect the adopted arrangement.
Paragraphs 11–19 and their footnotes inform the factual model but remain separate controls; their full requirements are not automatically incorporated into paragraph 10.
Oversight and operational evidence may bear on substantive responsibility, but the text does not define an exhaustive oversight checklist or impose strict liability for every incident.
Separate token holders, legal interests and beneficial interests are modeled only where the actual arrangement distinguishes them; no particular title structure is assumed.
This develops the substantive rivals already present in abstraction.32a0a2bca28a2d8f7a96e2de and abstraction.7679e9224a96a1b976663cff; it does not claim discovery of a wholly absent rival.

clauses.object: Substantive exercise of responsibility across components and ownership relationships

sources.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.
2 Product Providers are not expected to issue tokenised SFC-authorised investment products in bearer form.
(a)      the tokenisation arrangement6, particularly, with clear disclosure on whether off-chain or on-chain settlement is final;
(b)      the ownership representation of the tokens (eg, legal and beneficial title of the tokens, ownership of / interests in the product); and

Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and the integrity of the smart contracts5.

5 Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above and the smart contracts are not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.

Product Providers should confirm to the SFC that they have at least one competent staff with relevant experience and expertise to operate and/or supervise the tokenisation arrangement and to manage the new risks relating to ownership and technology appropriately.

sources.quote: This circular sets out the requirements under which the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) would consider allowing tokenisation of investment products authorised by the SFC under Part IV of the Securities and Futures Ordinance for offering to the public in Hong Kong.
B.   Requirements for primary dealing of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products

Product providers of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products (Product Providers) should ensure that the underlying products should meet the applicable requirements in the relevant rules and regulations, and product codes (including eligibility of Product Providers, product structure, investment and operational requirements, disclosure and ongoing compliance obligations).

Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should confirm to the SFC that they have at least one competent staff with relevant experience and expertise to operate and/or supervise the tokenisation arrangement and to manage the new risks relating to ownership and technology appropriately.

clauses.object: Paragraph 10 as retained responsibility coupled with substantive adequacy

sources.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.

Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and the integrity of the smart contracts5.

5 Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above and the smart contracts are not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.

Product Providers should confirm to the SFC that they have at least one competent staff with relevant experience and expertise to operate and/or supervise the tokenisation arrangement and to manage the new risks relating to ownership and technology appropriately.

clauses.warrant: This reading gives substantive effect to responsibility for soundness and records, strengthened by footnote 1's investor-ownership rationale and the later requirement to confirm and demonstrate soundness. In the outsourced-registrar case in r1, established material unreliability defeats this selected control despite effective oversight and acceptance of responsibility. Its strongest uncertainty is whether that conclusion imports separate performance duties into paragraph 10, whose immediate language focuses on who remains responsible. Neither the incident threshold nor any strict-liability consequence is supplied.

Outsourced performance remains possible, and supervision can be relevant; the source does not require the provider personally to execute every task.
The source does not establish that every operational incident necessarily breaches paragraph 10, or that reasonable care alone exhausts the duty.
No prior models were supplied. The challenge is to the first proposal’s limited allocation model: retained responsibility can coexist with inadequate oversight or defective records.
Argument evaluation is conditional on the retained source context

clauses.object: Paragraph 10 as substantive stewardship beyond retained responsibility

sources.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.

Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and the integrity of the smart contracts5.

Product Providers should, upon SFC’s request, obtain third party audit or verification on the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and integrity of the smart contracts.

5 Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above and the smart contracts are not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.

Product Providers should confirm to the SFC that they have at least one competent staff with relevant experience and expertise to operate and/or supervise the tokenisation arrangement and to manage the new risks relating to ownership and technology appropriately.

clauses.warrant: A provider could retain all three responsibility allocations yet lack effective supervision or have unreliable ownership records. The substantive reading therefore requires actors, component performance and continuing oversight evidence absent from the allocation predicate. It does not equate responsibility with personal performance or automatically impose strict liability.

sources.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

clauses.warrant: This reading treats paragraph 10 principally as allocating continuing responsibility, with concrete performance duties stated separately. Consider an outsourced registrar whose failure makes ownership records materially unreliable, although the Product Provider retained effective supervision, intervention capacity and accountability and promptly undertook remediation. That failure does not alone establish breach of paragraph 10 under this reading; the separate records duty may nevertheless be breached. Under r2, an established failure of proper record keeping also defeats the selected paragraph 10 control. Neither reading permits responsibility to be transferred to the registrar.

sources.quote: This circular sets out the requirements under which the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) would consider allowing tokenisation of investment products authorised by the SFC under Part IV of the Securities and Futures Ordinance for offering to the public in Hong Kong.

Tokenisation of investment products refers to the creation of blockchain-based tokens that represent or aim to represent ownership in an investment product. The tokenised product can then be recorded digitally on the blockchain, offered directly to end-investors, distributed by SFC-licensed intermediaries, or traded among the blockchain participants where allowed.
B.   Requirements for primary dealing of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products

Product providers of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products (Product Providers) should ensure that the underlying products should meet the applicable requirements in the relevant rules and regulations, and product codes (including eligibility of Product Providers, product structure, investment and operational requirements, disclosure and ongoing compliance obligations).

Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should confirm to the SFC that they have at least one competent staff with relevant experience and expertise to operate and/or supervise the tokenisation arrangement and to manage the new risks relating to ownership and technology appropriately.

sources.quote: Product providers of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products (Product Providers) should ensure that the underlying products should meet the applicable requirements in the relevant rules and regulations, and product codes (including eligibility of Product Providers, product structure, investment and operational requirements, disclosure and ongoing compliance obligations).

Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should confirm to the SFC that they have at least one competent staff with relevant experience and expertise to operate and/or supervise the tokenisation arrangement and to manage the new risks relating to ownership and technology appropriately.

sources.quote: Product providers of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products (Product Providers) should ensure that the underlying products should meet the applicable requirements in the relevant rules and regulations, and product codes (including eligibility of Product Providers, product structure, investment and operational requirements, disclosure and ongoing compliance obligations).

Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should confirm to the SFC that they have at least one competent staff with relevant experience and expertise to operate and/or supervise the tokenisation arrangement and to manage the new risks relating to ownership and technology appropriately.

Prior consultation is also required for tokenisation of existing SFC-authorised investment products and/or material changes to the tokenisation arrangements of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products. Such change(s) may require prior approval8.

8 For example, prior approval should be obtained before adding the disclosure of new tokenised unit/share class of an SFC-authorised fund in the Hong Kong offering documents and offering it to the public in Hong Kong. No prior approval is required for adding another tokenised unit/share class to the same fund if the tokenisation arrangement is substantially the same as the existing one.

sources.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.

Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and the integrity of the smart contracts5.

5 Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above and the smart contracts are not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.

Product Providers should confirm to the SFC that they have at least one competent staff with relevant experience and expertise to operate and/or supervise the tokenisation arrangement and to manage the new risks relating to ownership and technology appropriately.

clauses.standard: Meaning and evaluative predicates remain proposed
clauses.warrant: A materially stronger reading treats responsibility for management, operational soundness and records as requiring effective discharge as well as non-transferable accountability. Proper-records and assurance provisions support, but do not conclusively establish, this interpretation. Thus an outsourced failure could reveal a paragraph 10 deficiency even where accountability was never disclaimed. Both readings reject the same outsourcing-exemption hypothesis; the genuine rivalry concerns the content of responsibility, not an invented exception. The strongest uncertainty is the threshold for substantive failure: the source does not make every incident an automatic breach or impose an absolute guarantee.

clauses.object: Substantive exercise of responsibility across delegated operations

sources.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.

Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and the integrity of the smart contracts5.

5 Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above and the smart contracts are not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.

Product Providers should confirm to the SFC that they have at least one competent staff with relevant experience and expertise to operate and/or supervise the tokenisation arrangement and to manage the new risks relating to ownership and technology appropriately.

clauses.warrant: Review of the first model exposes a possible gap between retained accountability and effective exercise of responsibility. A provider could accept accountability on paper yet lack effective supervision of outsourced operations or ownership records. This rival could reject that arrangement under paragraph 10 itself. It does not infer that outsourcing is prohibited or that all operations must be performed internally.
